nodes.label: desktop memory - the NIM judge min_tokens fix

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. The RAGAS judge (_NimJudge in v3/eval/ragas.py, model qwen/qwen3.5-397b-a17b on NIM) sends min_tokens: 1 on every /chat/completions call. Without it, for some prompts this model greedily emits its end-of-turn token as the FIRST token, giving completion_tokens: 0, message.content: null and finish_reason: stop, so the verdict is empty and the eval cell errors with 'NIM judge returned null content'. It is deterministic at temperature 0 - the same input gives the same argmax and fails every run - so retrying or re-pacing never clears it, and raising temperature does not fix it because the end-of-turn token's probability dominates even at 0.7, verified. min_tokens: 1 forces at least one generated token and the model then writes the full verdict JSON, verified live on the exact failing prompt at 0 to 107 tokens. A safety net in the same code dumps the full raw response to judge_null_dumps.jsonl on still-empty content and fails loud. It is not thinking-mode related: the endpoint defaults enable_thinking off and reasoning_content came back null or empty too, so the model genuinely generated zero tokens
